Component.Text: When a widget needs to look different from anything a style sheet can do, C++ can take over its drawing and leave everything else as it was. When no widget does the job, C++ can register a component of your own as a new element. Either way, the XML uses them like any other element.
jive::LookAndFeel::addPainter() draws every Slider.segmented with a C++ function. They're still Sliders, attached to the gain and pan parameters, and the theme still picks their colours.

XYPad is a juce::Component, added to the interpreter's ComponentFactory so views can use <XYPad>. A decorator keeps its x-value and y-value attributes in sync and triggers on-change, and a type predicate lets style sheets select it by name.
